tools.name: nogpu_status
tools.description:
A job's status, and its report once ready (same fields as nogpu_report). Also shows download_url after
        payment: GET it with header X-Claim-Token. claim_token and report_url are secrets.

tools.name: nogpu_buy
tools.description: Read-only, never pays: for a certified (fit) report, returns the $99 offer to keep the model, the question to ask the user word for word and a card checkout link for the user. If the job is not buyable, returns the reason.

tools.name: nogpu_delete
tools.description:
Delete an uploaded job's data now (otherwise deleted within 24h, or 24h after payment if you bought the
        model).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: nogpu_report · Private data: nogpu_report, nogpu_status · Public sink: nogpu_report · Destructive: nogpu_report, nogpu_delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: nogpu_report · Private data: nogpu_report, nogpu_status · Public sink: nogpu_report · Destructive: nogpu_report, nogpu_delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

detail: Tool "nogpu_report" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
